subject: Interview rotation plan and scenario-focused anchors for Staff LLM Serving
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Interview rotation plan and scenario-focused anchors for Staff LLM Serving

Team —

Thanks for agreeing to help run the loop for our Staff LLM Serving candidate (Samantha Lee). Per the hiring sheet, she is scheduled for on-site (virtual) interviews next week; this thread is to lock the rotation and call out the scenario-focused anchors each interviewer should prioritize. Goal: make interviews tightly scoped so we get signal on architecture judgment, latency/cost tradeoffs, and runtime operational reasoning.

Proposed rotation (45 + 15 debrief slots):
- 09:00 — System design: Markus (lead) — focus on model sharding/kv-cache strategy, throughput SLOs
- 10:00 — Serving runtime internals: Marissa — focus on kernel selection, quantization, and perf debugging
- 11:00 — Product & tradeoffs: Laura — focus on SLA design, fallback policies, and customer-oriented tradeoffs
- 14:00 — Culture / leadership / execution: me (Karthik) — team/roadmap judgment and hiring fit

Anchors for each interviewer (short bullets to keep consistency):
- System design (Markus): expect a 20–25 minute vertical on a real-case sequence-length distribution; ask candidate to sketch data flow & failure modes, then probe for mitigations and measurable SLOs.
- Runtime internals (Marissa): include a short kernel-performance debugging exercise; candidate should explain tradeoffs for int8 vs 4-bit quant and KV cache eviction heuristics.
- Product (Laura): give a customer scenario where latency spikes in one region; candidate should propose routing/rollback/fallback and cost implications.
- Exec/culture (Karthik): focus on hiring rubric signals and cross-team alignment examples.

Prep materials attached: candidate-pack.pdf (resume + coding sample), and a short debrief template. I also created a shared doc with example question prompts: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcDef-Interview-anchors

Please confirm you can own the assigned slot and whether you want to swap any anchors. If none, I’ll send calendar invites and the rotation .ics.

Thanks —
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Hiring Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

I can take the runtime internals slot. Two quick asks to increase signal:
1) For the kernel-intro exercise, please ask her to estimate token throughput for a simple attention block on an A100 and justify the dominant bottleneck — I want to see if she can reason from first principles rather than reciting best practices.
2) Add a short prompt about debugging a regression after a model quant change (what telemetry would she check first?).

Happy to land on the exact questions in the shared doc. I also have a short perf micro-benchmark I can send (one-pager).

Thanks — I’m good for the system design slot. A couple of small tweaks from my side:

- Swap order so the candidate sees runtime internals before system design? It helps because runtime details will inform design choices; if Marissa is okay, I suggest 09:00 Marissa (runtime), 10:00 Markus (system design).
- For system design I’ll use a two-part scenario: (A) design for a steady-state high-throughput batch workload; (B) extension to tight-latency interactive use with cold-start constraints. This will make it easier to check both throughput & latency thinking.

Also: I volunteer to be bar-raiser for this loop unless you have a different suggestion. If I play bar-raiser I’ll take the debrief owner role and grade consistency across anchors.

-Markus

All —

Thanks for the quick responses and the swaps — rotation is locked as below (final calendar invites sent to Samantha and the loop):
- 09:00 PT — Runtime internals (Marissa)
- 10:00 PT — System design (Markus)
- 11:00 PT — Product & tradeoffs (Laura)
- 14:00 PT — Exec / culture / hiring fit (Karthik)

Markus will act as bar-raiser and own the debrief. I attached the debrief-template.md and a short scoring matrix — please use the shared doc to enter brief notes right after each session (2–3 bullets + score 1–5 per anchor).

Quick reminder on expectations: keep questions practical and avoid multi-hour design asks; we get better signal from narrower scenarios and detailed follow-ups. If anyone needs to swap, alert me by EOD Monday so we can notify the candidate.

Thanks again — looking forward to a crisp loop.

Karthik
